note: P4297 (Pro 27:10) — do not forsake a friend; better a near neighbour than a far brother.

dims.v: proximate loyalty — a near neighbour worth more than a distant brother
the judgement that a neighbour who is near is better, in the day of calamity, than a brother far away — the value of steadfast, close friendship over distant kinship
the near, faithful friend prized above the far-off kinsman

tob (better) — 'BETTER is a neighbor who is near than a brother who is far away'; in trouble, a faithful friend at hand is worth more than a brother at a distance. Cultivated, proximate friendship is a treasure not to be forsaken (cf 18:24; 17:17).
